items.title: What Would It Take For Eli Lilly Stock To Keep Climbing?
items.summary: Eli Lilly (LLY) trades near $1,150, up about 52% over the past year, and is now worth more than a trillion dollars. At that size the easy read is that the big money has been made. But Lilly has barely started selling Foundayo, its oral obesity medicine, outside the United States. So how much is left? The scenario below starts from Lilly's own trailing numbers, but the growth, margin, and multiple it assumes are ours. It is not a forecast and not a price target.

items.title: Is Johnson & Johnson Stock Expensive, Or Is STELARA Hiding The Real Price?
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) stock has returned about 57% over the past year, against about 17% for the S&P 500. On the earnings it has already banked, that price looks expensive. But those earnings carry STELARA, which is losing share to biosimilar competition. What looks dear on earnings already reported comes down sharply on the earnings analysts expect.

items.title: Merck Stock Nearly Doubled Without A Change In Its Revenue Growth
items.summary: Merck (MRK) stock returned about 87% over the past twelve months, climbing from roughly $79 to about $147. Nothing in the year's results looks like that. The medicines Merck sells today grew at their usual pace. Investors spent the year repricing what comes next.

items.title: Can AstraZeneca's Broad Pipeline Offset Recent Setbacks?
items.summary: AZN's pipeline setbacks weigh on its stock, but a deep late-stage pipeline and 20+ expected readouts offer key catalysts.

items.title: J&J Up 18% in Three Months: Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
items.summary: JNJ's growth gets a boost from new drug launches and pipeline wins, but Stelara's patent loss and MedTech headwinds remain key risks.

items.title: The Moneymaxxing Crowd Will Love 5 High-Yield Dividend Stocks Under $20
items.summary: Younger investors are rewriting the rules of wealth building, and five overlooked dividend stocks under $20 sit right at the center of that shift. The real question is whether these picks can hold up long enough to matter.

items.title: Can Intuitive Surgical Make Up For A Lower Price Per Surgery?
items.summary: Intuitive Surgical (ISRG) has lost about 12% over the past year, while the S&P 500 returned about 17%. Most of the debate has been about the U.S. procedure growth slowing. The number that should worry a holder more is the money the company collects on the instruments used in each operation. Intuitive plans to lower it.

items.title: Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) Faces A Fresh Valuation Test On DePuy Sale Talk
items.summary: A potential sale of DePuy Synthes for about US$20b has put Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) back in focus for investors watching how management reshapes its MedTech footprint and capital allocation priorities. The share price of Johnson & Johnson sits at US$270.22 after a 1-day share price return of 1.10% and a 90-day share price return of 18.32%.
